messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: HIGH - GeoDNS anomaly detected in eu-west-1 affecting resolution for api.redwood.ai — page sent to oncall Mia.

Mia (oncall): Got it, paging in. Seeing a spike of 5xx from EU customers in our error dashboard.

Rohit (sre): I'm on dig/traceroute now. Quick check shows different public resolvers returning divergent answers.

Taylor (netops): From perf probes we're seeing Route53 returning stale/partial answers to some client prefixes, while Cloudflare edges still have older cached A records.

Mia (oncall): Can someone paste the dig output?

Rohit (sre): ```
$ dig +short A api.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
54.12.34.56
$ dig +short A api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
NXDOMAIN
$ dig +short NS api.redwood.ai @198.51.100.2
ns-geo1.example.net.
```

Taylor (netops): Confirmed. Cloudflare probe shows cached global IP, some upstream resolvers are returning NXDOMAIN for the geo record set. Looks like Route53 geo failover considered eu endpoint unhealthy and returned nothing to certain resolvers.

Alex (eng-runtime): Could be our healthcheck agent on eu-proxy flapped and triggered failover. If TTLs are low, propagation flips will be visible as inconsistent answers across resolvers.

Mia (oncall): Impact summary: elevated 5xx and client-side DNS errors for EU region causing retries and increased latency. CS ticket inbound from a large customer.

Jenny (cust-succ): ACME reported intermittent DNS failures starting ~08:35 UTC, they saw SDK-level connection errors. They're asking for ETA — I'll hold until we have a mitigation.

Rohit (sre): Proposed mitigation sequence: 1) restart eu healthcheck agent (to prevent further false-unhealthy flips) 2) temporarily disable Route53 geo failover so records respond consistently 3) purge Cloudflare edge cache if stale answers persist. Doing step 1 now.

Taylor (netops): Starting Cloudflare purge API call now: `curl -s -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/<zone>/purge_cache" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"purge_everything":true}'` — returning success.

Mia (oncall): Rohit, can you toggle the Route53 failover? If we need AWS support, flag it.

Rohit (sre): Route53 failover toggled to static routing (round-robin) at 08:43:12 UTC. Change propagated to control plane; DNS TTL is 60s so external caches will refresh shortly.

Rohit (sre): Healthcheck agent restarted on eu-proxy at 08:42:50 UTC, logs indicate agent OOM during spike; restarted with adjusted probe concurrency.

Taylor (netops): Our external DNS probes show NXDOMAIN rate dropping. Cloudflare purge completed at 08:44:03 UTC.

Alex (eng-runtime): I pushed temporary weights to prefer global endpoint to avoid oscillation while we stabilize. Will rollback after 30m.

Mia (oncall): Jenny, any confirmation from ACME?

Jenny (cust-succ): ACME confirms errors reduced and can reach service again as of ~08:46 UTC. They're asking for a short explanation for their internal postmortem — I'll provide a summary once we have timeline.

Rohit (sre): Observed reduction in 5xxs and DNS NXDOMAINs across EU probes. Setting watch for 1 hour. Root cause candidate: healthcheck agent OOM causing false-unhealthy signal -> Route53 geo failover -> inconsistent answers across resolvers + Cloudflare stale cache.

Mia (oncall): Next steps: 1) brief postmortem with timeline + diffs for healthcheck config 2) add synthetic cross-provider DNS check to run every 5m (verify CF vs R53 answers) 3) increase healthcheck agent resilience (memory guard). Assigning Rohit to lead the PM and Taylor to add synthetic check.

Rohit (sre): Will own the PM and collect dig/traceroute logs + Cloudflare purge timestamps.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV2 at 08:50:00 UTC — monitoring for 60 minutes.

Mia (oncall): Thanks everyone. Handoff to next oncall in 30m. :thumbsup:
